$sources: The species: Narcissus poeticus L., pheasant's-eye: a bulb, the leaves linear, 20-45 cm by 6-10 mm; a single flower 4.5-7 cm on a scape, the perianth white, spreading, the corona a shallow cup, yellow with a red rim; flowering April to May, the leaves dying back by June (C. Stace, New Flora of the British Isles, 4th ed., Cambridge 2019, Amaryllidaceae).
The bulbs at the Hall of Light's plotted points (the as-built orchard, HallOfLightPlanting.swift), heights 0.20-0.35.
name: Narcissus poeticus
note: Out of flower in June, its leaves yellowing as they die back after flowering. The museum shows it in early summer, Mangzhong to Xiazhi (June).
